executiveSummary: GM0770 passes the deterministic execution contract for all ten canonical scenarios, T+0/6/12/24/48/72 and all eight essential services. Its official 2025 identity, generalized boundary, 20,389 residents, 24 neighbourhoods, six BAG places and arithmetic are coherent. Current NWB handling also correctly limits three verified A67/N397 logical links to Mobility and road logistics/Supply. Release is nevertheless correction-required. The regional safety authority states that high-lying Brabant-Zuidoost has no direct flood danger, while the Rhine/Meuse/IJssel preset creates 1.441351 m-equivalent internal flood stress through T+72, labels the public hero 96 percent inundation stress and leaves 10,566 Eersel residents under pressure without a selected local water or defence event. Nine nonzero hazard families reuse one exact 24-neighbourhood ordering. This contradicts official local evidence: the municipal sewer plan identifies two specific cloudburst bottleneck groups, the climate plan separates urban heat from rural groundwater decline, and an official combustible-nature polygon/source inside Knegsel-Oeyenbos ranks that source neighbourhood last in a controlled fire test. The public water-register snapshot contains six sewer pumps, one surface-water pump and 70 weirs, whereas the municipal plan describes 483 pump units and 107.2 km of pressure sewer; neither inventory supplies live connectivity or state. At T+24 to T+72 the compound run freezes all eight service availabilities, pressure and 13,733 affected residents despite rain/wind ending and cyber disruption falling. Public official data can improve scenario selection and context, but observations, registers, provider territories and plans must remain separate from simulated T+72 state, and NoData/no match must never become zero or safe.

Reference point [5.3268101713177805, 51.37313103033667] lies inside the generalized 2025 municipality geometry.

geography.summary: The generalized municipality and 24-neighbourhood geometry is coherent, but it cannot substitute for Kleine Beerze/Run catchments, sewer drainage, combustible-nature, service-zone or incident geometry.
notes: BoundaryEdition and statisticsEdition both equal 2025; six official BAG places are Duizel, Eersel, Knegsel, Steensel, Vessem and Wintelre.
Thirty-one BRT settlement labels comprise six woonkernen, four deelkernen, six gehuchten and fifteen buurtschappen; labels are context rather than population or response zones.

The municipal plans distinguish Eersel core rain/heat mechanisms from rural groundwater and water-system patterns around Vessem, Knegsel and Wintelre. The common neighbourhood seed does not preserve those mechanisms.
Administrative polygons, water-control points, risk polygons, provider territories, road sections and incident footprints retain separate provenance and cannot be conflated.

demography.summary: Headline population and aggregate vulnerability inputs agree with CBS 2025 and neighbourhood totals reconcile within official publication rounding.
notes: Twenty-four independently rounded neighbourhood rows sum to 20,400 residents, eleven above the municipality total, a +0.054 percent publication-rounding difference; they sum to 8,735 households and 5,030 residents aged 65 or older.
The model transparently reconciles neighbourhood population back to the official 20,389 municipality total; this allocation is not a revision of CBS observations.

Population, household form, age, density, land/water and accessibility can support aggregate vulnerability/service-demand context but do not identify individual medical dependence, present location, preparedness or emergency priority.
Suppressed, unknown, not-applicable and incomplete values remain null rather than zero.

regionalDetail.summary: Twenty-four neighbourhoods provide useful social and land-use context, but field gaps and a hazard-independent allocator prevent operational prioritization.

Official rain bottlenecks geocode to BU07700000 Eersel-kom en Lindeakkers and BU07700002 Eersel-Zuid, but they rank ninth and sixth in the modeled pluvial map.

Official combustible-nature polygons include Heieinden, Buikheide-Oude Molen, Molenvelden, Oeienbos, Heersche Heide, Oostelbeersche Heide, De Donksbergen and Boksheide; static eligibility does not imply an incident or current fuel state.
Compound T+24 local population, affected population and all eight service demand/delivery totals reconcile while all nine nonzero hazard maps retain one exact ordering.

settlements.summary: Six BAG woonplaatsen and differentiated BRT settlement labels represent Eersel's polycentric rural municipality without fabricating population or service zones.
notes: Duizel, Eersel, Knegsel, Steensel, Vessem and Wintelre are the six in-boundary BAG place records; none of their reference centres falls outside the generalized boundary.
BRT woonkern/deelkern/gehucht/buurtschap labels provide orientation around the six main cores and rural places but do not carry CBS population or emergency-response semantics.
Place centres and settlement labels are not evacuation areas, shelters, service districts, catchments or live occupancy.

transport.summary: Three A67/N397 logical links have coherent current road provenance and correct service scope, but static geometry does not establish incident-time access or external-care continuity.
notes: Generated logical routes are A67 toward Bladel, A67 toward Veldhoven and N397 toward Bergeijk, backed by seventeen distinct NWB wvk identifiers and no duplicate source id.

The current engine includes those three links only for Mobility and Supply and includes zero NWB routes for power, water, drainage, gas, telecom or facilities. Nominal 260/150 values remain synthetic logical transfer capacity, not measured traffic throughput.

No ProRail station lies inside GM0770; 34 scheduled transit stop-area records are deployment context. Static NWB, ProRail and GTFS cannot prove a road open, bus operating, evacuation throughput, repair travel or ambulance route at T+0–72.

A deployed NDW current snapshot contained two in-boundary incident points on 2 September 2026. Those valid-time observations are display-only and route-unmatched; they cannot be projected into an arbitrary scenario T+72.

emergencyContext.summary: Strong public water, provider, telecom, education and external-care context exists, but complete topology, incident state and response resources do not.
notes: The municipal sewer plan lists 483 pump units, 107.2 km pressure sewer, three overflows, three emergency overflows, two bergbezinkbassins, six bergbezinkleidingen and about 8,250 gullies; it explicitly says actual pump capacity remains to be tested at 35 locations.

Exact point-in-polygon intersection with deployed HWH data finds 77 records: six sewer pumps, one surface-water pump and 70 weirs. This partial national public snapshot does not reproduce the municipal inventory and neither source supplies live connectivity or operation.

Mijn Aansluiting identifies Enexis electricity/gas, Brabant Water drinking water and Ziggo media at the reference point; drainage returns no feature. Territories identify responsibility, not complete coverage, topology, capacity, outage or restoration.

The deployment contains 42 RDI antenna installations, twelve active DUO education-location records and no in-boundary RIVM emergency department. Nearest acute-care record is Máxima Medisch Centrum Veldhoven at 7.34 km straight-line; none of these facts establishes coverage, shelter role, access, staffing or incident capacity.

No authorized complete feeder, pressure-zone, sewer-catchment/RWZI, gas, telecom-backhaul, care-route, pharmacy/food/fuel stock, priority-customer, crew, vehicle, pump-control, backup or restoration dataset is loaded or inferred.

T+24 local allocation reconciles population, affected population and all eight demand/delivery balances. Maximum observed floating-point discrepancy is 1.0658141036401503e-14.
Changing among all eleven map layers leaves hazard, municipal pressure and affected population invariant; maximum observed local hazard delta is zero.

spatialPlausibility.summary: One shared neighbourhood hash, an implausible direct-river screen and failed source containment conflict with Eersel's published rain, water, heat/drought and nature-fire geography.
notes: Current packages/sim-core/src/model.ts seeds local hazard without hazard-specific selected geometry or source containment. Severe storm, pluvial, river, coastal, heat, winter, cyber, wildfire and compound consequently share one exact 24-neighbourhood order.

For pluvial T+24, official hotspot BU07700000 Eersel-kom en Lindeakkers ranks ninth at 0.213443 and BU07700002 Eersel-Zuid ranks sixth at 0.224755; Bedrijventerrein Eersel ranks first despite no selected local rain/depth surface.

A controlled source [5.36276824428771, 51.39447434193721] lies inside official Oeienbos and BU07700501 Knegsel-Oeyenbos. At T+24 the model creates direct fire 0.465008, smoke 0.456718 and severity 0.471102, yet the containing neighbourhood ranks last at 0.397090 while Bedrijventerrein Eersel ranks first at 0.539377.

The current regional profile says the high region has no direct flood danger, yet the major-river preset generates 1.441351 internal flood stress and 96 percent normalized UI inundation stress without a selected local flood pathway.
GM0770 has no municipality-specific unsupported-spatial note, so the browser renders precise local ranks, affected counts and service values without an Eersel-specific audit warning.

River T+24 availability is power 0.438555, water 0.418262, drainage 0.276608, gas 0.685675, telecom 0.409707, mobility 0.793982, facilities 0.574288 and supply 0.579896. At T+72 facilities alone falls further to 0.375988 while the unselected direct-river field persists.

Compound T+24 availability is power 0.383665, water 0.359399, drainage 0.307068, gas 0.585768, telecom 0.219237, mobility 0.407877, facilities 0.365368 and supply 0.460605. These values repeat exactly at T+72 and are generic scenario/dependency outputs, not operator estimates.

Official sources support plausible dependency directions among electricity, telecom, drinking water, surface-water/sewer pumping, A67/N397 access, external acute care and emergency supply, but none calibrates exact demands, deliveries, reserves, backups, damage, queues or restoration.

The graph contains no named Enexis feeder/gas zone, Brabant Water pressure area, telecom backhaul, sewer-pump/catchment/receiving-water/RWZI chain, hospital acceptance route, shelter role, food/fuel depot or crew base. Unavailable authorized or security-sensitive topology remains Unknown.
NWB Mobility/Supply snapshots are logical transfer proxies. Their nominal capacities are scenario ceilings, not measured road or logistics throughput.

causalTrace.summary: Hazard, service and municipal ledgers close arithmetically and expose evidence class, dependency order, operational assumptions and counterfactual scope.
notes: Hazard contributions sum to headline severity; every service baseline plus exact-stage deltas sums to availability; weighted service shortfalls sum to municipal pressure.
System-pressure weights are power 0.18, water 0.15, drainage 0.08, gas 0.09, telecom 0.12, mobility 0.12, facilities 0.14 and supply 0.12, totaling one.
Dependency chains, local-context factors, drivers, recovery progress and restore-service counterfactual deltas are finite and arithmetically closed.

Household preparedness affects modeled people/supply consequences rather than physical fragility. Day type, start clock, demand, backup, network and repair multipliers are normalized and labeled scenario assumptions; interventions are response-delayed and do not masquerade as actual Eersel crews/assets.

Event-attributable essential-service person-hours integrate weighted unmet-service pressure relative to a matched no-event baseline before intermunicipal transfers and apply a preparedness multiplier. They are a modeled pre-transfer burden proxy, not observed outage-hours, casualties, displacement or welfare loss.
Arithmetic explainability does not validate the spatial seed, direct-river field, infrastructure topology or recovery calibration identified in the open findings.

recovery72h.summary: Recovery guards are numerically coherent, but Eersel's sustained river and compound trajectories have no selected event, asset/access condition or response-resource evidence.
notes: Canonical river stress/severity remain 1.441351/0.452977 from T+24 through T+72. Pressure rises 0.480051 to 0.507813, affected population rises 9,769 to 10,566 and cumulative proxy person-hours rise 172,565.76 to 704,358.95 without a selected water boundary, defence state, arrival, duration, recession or pump operation.

Compound severity falls from 0.840288 at T+24 to 0.299966 at T+72, rain and wind end and cyber disruption drops from 0.506926 to 0.065931, yet pressure stays 0.618068, affected residents stay 13,733 and every service availability is identical.

Municipal and water-board plans describe pump testing, telemetry, storage, drought and water-system projects, but supply no event-valid dewatering, access, backup, crew, material, mutual-aid or restoration schedule for this run.

Headless Chromium at 1440×1000 selected Eersel, the river preset and T+72 and traversed all eleven layers without page, console or local HTTP errors. It displayed 'Scenario severity 96% inundation stress · evidence class derived-screening' without an Eersel-specific unsupported warning.
Rendering and generic evidence-class labels do not validate magnitude, timing or restoration. Until selected source/resource evidence exists, the trajectory is a non-operational sensitivity only.

evidenceSources.title: Verbreed Gemeentelijk Rioleringsplan Eersel 2023–2027
supports: The municipal BRP2020/stress-test process identified about twenty bottlenecks and names two groups with much modeled water nuisance: Kerkstraat/Carquefouplein/Gebroeders Hoeksstraat in Eersel-kom en Lindeakkers and Hoolstraat near Sporthal De Kraanvogel in Eersel-Zuid. Two locations also experienced nuisance in 2021.

The plan distinguishes 70 mm in one hour T100 and 90 mm in one hour for vital/vulnerable functions, with explicit depth/duration bands: nuisance below two hours and ten centimetres, severe nuisance above ten centimetres or two hours, and overlast above twenty centimetres.

Its 2022 inventory lists 483 pump units, 107.2 km pressure sewer, three overflows, three emergency overflows, two bergbezinkbassins, six bergbezinkleidingen and about 8,250 gullies. It says actual pump capacity is not known and proposes testing 35 locations.

Main pumps/edge facilities were telemetered while individual pump units used a red warning lamp. This fixed plan is not a current alarm/state feed and does not expose complete connectivity, pump curves, backup, receiving levels or T+72 operation.

The human-readable regulation has no stable operational API, fixed update cadence or explicit standalone reuse licence for underlying native stress-test rasters. Obtain owner-authorized native exports with event, edition, units, resolution, lineage, licence and NoData before causal ingestion.

evidenceSources.title: Duurzaamheidsbeleid 2017–2025 and municipal climate-adaptation context
evidenceSources.edition: Static policy horizon 2017–2025; climate-adaptation page inspected 2 September 2026
supports: The policy's light climate stress test identifies tropical-night/heat sensitivity in the built-up cores, including parts of Eersel with roughly two to three weeks per year in its future context.

It separately describes projected groundwater decline of about 20–30 cm around Vessem, Knegsel and Wintelre and more than 30 cm north of Wintelre. This is planning/scenario context, not a current groundwater observation or a 72-hour forecast.

The current municipal overview https://www.eersel.nl/klimaatadaptatie recognizes extreme rain, flooding, heat and drought as local adaptation themes but provides no machine-readable event surface or live state.

The distinct heat and groundwater patterns falsify an interpretation of one common 24-neighbourhood rank as locally validated heat/drought exposure. Native products require edition, scenario, temperature/PET/groundwater semantics, units, resolution, licence and NoData before use.

evidenceSources.title: Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2025–2028
supports: The profile states that the high-lying region has no direct flood danger, while a large-river dike failure to the north can indirectly prevent Brabant water from draining. Direct inundation and blocked-drainage pathways must therefore remain distinct.

It identifies power, ICT and telecom outage as high-impact risks and notes extensive forest/heath, recreation and nature-fire exposure. It also recognizes extreme rain, cold/snow/ice, heat, storm, gas/water/wastewater disruption and cyber cascades.

The A67 is identified as a major freight artery and Eindhoven Airport as a regional dependency. The document supplies regional mechanisms, not Eersel route passability, local service topology, operator state, crews, resources or exact restoration times.

This statutory planning PDF has no operational API/fixed cadence and no explicit standard reuse licence on the publication. It structures exercises; it is not a forecast, probability, current outage or validation of exact municipal model values.

Named Eersel-area mechanisms include Hoogeind as a historic bottleneck, Molenbroek floodplain and Dorp aan de Beek Vessem. These are local catchment/programme contexts absent from the generic named-major-river field.

Current pages https://www.dommel.nl/seizoensupdates-2026 and https://www.dommel.nl/klein-laagje-water-op-de-kleine-beerze-en-beekloop-om-waterleven-te-redden describe exceptional 2026 drought and survival water pumped to Beerze/Beekloop. They are timestamped present context, not arbitrary scenario forcing or a T+72 forecast.

Public project/update pages have no stable machine operational endpoint or explicit standard reuse licence. Owner-authorized water-level/flow, structure-state and scenario products require valid time, quality, units, coverage and NoData before causal use.

evidenceSources.publisher: HWH / PDOK / Mijn Aansluiting / Netbeheer Nederland / RDI / DUO / RIVM / KNMI / RWS / NDW
evidenceSources.title: Integration-ready public water, provider, planning, facility and valid-time observation context for Eersel
evidenceSources.edition: Deployed public-context snapshots retrieved 2 September 2026; every source retains its own edition and valid time
supports: HWH IMWA at the cited URL and DAMO at https://api.pdok.nl/hwh/waterschappen-waterketen-damo/ogc/v1 are national OGC APIs under CC BY-SA 4.0; GWSW at https://api.pdok.nl/rioned/waterschappen-waterketen-gwsw/ogc/v1 is CC0. This signals possible external dependency, not route, acceptance or capacity.

KNMI Data Platform https://developer.dataplatform.knmi.nl/ provides product-specific valid-time weather/forecast data, commonly CC BY 4.0, with radar products around five-minute cadence. KNMI FDSN https://rdsa.knmi.nl/fdsnws/event/1 is automatically updated and defaults to CC BY 4.0. The deployment assigns zero weather stations and zero 365-day seismic origins to GM0770; this is sparse/no-match coverage, not zero hazard.

RWS Waterinfo https://waterinfo.rws.nl/api/point/latestmeasurement?parameterId=waterhoogte is generally ten-minute, five-minute-cached, CC0 and non-mission-critical; GM0770 has zero assigned observation points. NDW DATEX II https://opendata.ndw.nu/actueel_beeld.xml.gz is CC0 current-picture data and the deployed snapshot has two in-boundary event points. Both require source/valid time and quality, cannot define arbitrary T+72 state, and a no-match never means zero/safe/open.

RWS climate atlas WMS https://geo.rijkswaterstaat.nl/services/ogc/gdr/klimaat_effect_atlas/ows exposes CC0 layer bij_70mm_per_2uur, catalogue updated 5 August 2026. It is national scenario context with a different 70 mm/two-hour event from the municipal 70 mm/one-hour test; coverage/NoData and event semantics must remain visible and it is not a forecast.

findings.summary: The major-river preset presents critical direct Eersel inundation despite authoritative regional evidence that the high region has no direct flood danger.
findings.evidence: E05 states that Brabant-Zuidoost has no direct flood danger and distinguishes the indirect pathway in which a northern large-river failure prevents Brabant water draining. The canonical Rhine/Meuse/IJssel preset instead holds internal flood stress 1.441351 and severity 0.452977 from T+24 through T+72, reports 9,769 then 10,566 affected residents, and selects no Kleine Beerze/Run, receiving-water, defence, connected footprint, arrival, duration, recession or pump state. Headless Chromium at Eersel/T+72 displays 'Scenario severity 96% inundation stress · evidence class derived-screening' without a municipality-specific warning.
findings.action: Before release suppress direct named-major-river amplitude for GM0770, mark local river magnitude/ranks/derivative services unsupported and show the result only as a non-operational sensitivity. residualLimitations: This is a deterministic planning-model audit, not validation against an observed Eersel disaster, outage, evacuation, casualty, health, welfare or restoration dataset.
CBS/PDOK 2025 generalized boundaries support municipal aggregation but not parcel hydraulics, Kleine Beerze/Run catchments, sewer zones, fire perimeters, utility zones or incident access.

The municipal 2022 sewer plan and 2017–2025 sustainability policy are fixed planning sources; their named locations and scenarios are not current observations, warnings, asset telemetry or T+72 forecasts.
The VRBZO profile supplies regional mechanism and risk context, not event probabilities, local forcing, resource inventories or restoration promises.

HWH IMWA/DAMO/GWSW is partial provider-supplied inventory; record count, capacity field and status do not establish complete coverage, compatible units, connectivity, direction, operation, backup or service delivery.
IPO combustible-nature polygons are eligibility/planning context with old begin-validity dates, not live fuel, ignition, incident perimeter or suppression state.
NWB/ProRail/GTFS and a current NDW snapshot do not provide complete local-road, bus, evacuation, ambulance, repair-access or future passability state.
Provider/capacity/antenna/school/care records are partial dated context, not complete topology, current load, coverage, occupancy, criticality, backup, stock, access or restoration commitment.

Zero assigned KNMI weather stations, seismic origins, RIVM PM2.5 stations or RWS Waterinfo observations means sparse/no-match coverage, never zero weather, seismicity, pollution, water level or threat.

No reviewed safe public source supplies complete Enexis, Brabant Water, sewer/treatment, gas, telecom/backhaul, facility, food/fuel or emergency-resource topology/state; unavailable or security-sensitive detail was not inferred.

First-72-hour household behavior, medically dependent residents, commuters/visitors, responders, mutual aid, shelters, buses, pharmacies, fuel/food stocks, pump controls, crew travel and repair priorities remain scenario assumptions or Unknown.
